openai.sample_unit: kidney stone spectra in the prospective quality-assurance cohort
models_evaluated: Internally developed FTIR spectra classification suite, including a convolutional neural network and constituent-specific models

links.outcome: Detection and correction of erroneous laboratory reports in the human–AI workflow
links.effect: Corrected reports increased from 1.22 to 9.57 per 10,000 spectra (RR, 7.87; 95% CI, 4.08-15.2); AI identified 62 additional errors.
links.quote: As is shown, the overall rate of misreported kidney stone spectra in the study period was nearly 8 times higher than that in the 1 year before initiating the program (RR, 7.87; 95% CI, 4.08-15.2).

links.outcome: Concordance among predictions selected for automatic classification versus secondary human review
links.effect: Concordance was 98.7% (95% CI, 98.56%-98.9%) for autoPass candidates versus 84.3% (95% CI, 84.0%-84.6%) for cases flagged for manual secondary review.
links.quote: When the stone spectra were grouped into those stones selected for autoPass (candidate for automatic classification) and those not selected (flagged for manual secondary review), the concordance rates were 98.7% (95% CI, 98.56%-98.9%) and 84.3% (95% CI, 84.0%-84.6%), respectively.

links.outcome: Concordance in initial validation versus prospective clinical deployment
links.effect: Initial validation concordance was 95.2% (95% CI, 94.9%-95.5%); prospective clinical concordance was 90.0% (95% CI, 89.8%-90.2%).
links.quote: The AI algorithm and technologist provided concordant interpretations on 73,388 (90.0%; 95% CI, 89.8%-90.2%) clinical kidney stone spectra ( Table 1 ).

unlisted_practices: AI quality-assurance overreads of human laboratory interpretations, with independent technologist adjudication of discordances and correction of verified reporting errors.

links.effect: The report revision rate was nearly 8 times higher during the AI implementation period compared to the control period (RR 7.9, 95% CI 4.1-15.2).
links.quote: The report revision rate during the AI implementation period was nearly 8 times higher than that during the control period (relative risk, 7.9; 95% CI, 4.1-15.2).
